"""Everything through the language model: memories of how the work went, read by the model that serves each request.

Nothing here serves a request without the model, and nothing here asks Jev. It is where a search starts when the
question is whether a search can find the code that moves work from the model to a decision program.
"""

KINDS_PROMPT = """{contract}

Below are runs where the assistant, a language model, handled requests for
this job: each request, every tool call with its result, and the verdict.
Some requests are worded oddly, some should not be acted on at all, and
some runs went wrong.

List the kinds of request these runs show, and for each write what the
assistant should know the next time it meets one: how ids are really
written in the tools, which tools to call and in what order, and the
mistakes to avoid. Use as few kinds as cover the runs.

Reply with only a JSON list. Each item has the keys "name" (short, in
snake_case), "description" (which requests belong to this kind, and which
similar ones don't), "guidance" (what the assistant should know), and
"acts" (true if a request of this kind should end in an action, false if
it should only be answered or passed on).

{episodes}"""

ROUTER = """async def decide(request, kit):
    found = await kit.recall(request, k=1)
    if len(found) == 0:
        return {"handoff": "nothing learned applies"}
    return {"serve": found[0]["name"]}
"""


async def learn(lab):
    if len(lab.memories) > 0:
        for memory in lab.memories:
            lab.remember(**memory)
        return ROUTER
    shown = "\n\n".join(lab.render(e) for e in lab.episodes)
    reply = await lab.ask(lab.fill(KINDS_PROMPT, contract=lab.contract, episodes=shown))
    for kind in lab.parse(reply):
        lab.remember(kind["name"], kind["description"], kind["guidance"], route="none", read_only=not kind["acts"])
    return ROUTER

MEMORIES = [
    {'name': 'book_one_meeting', 'description': "Requests to put exactly one meeting on this week's calendar with named people, a length, a day window and usually a start or end limit. They may be chatty, terse or in shorthand ('grab 30 min', 'sched req: ...', 'need slot this wk', 'one mtg'). Not this kind: requests for two meetings or 'twice', requests that only ask for availability or say not to book, and cancel, move, hold or draft requests.", 'route': 'none', 'read_only': False, 'body': """Make two calls: find_shared_starts, then book_time.

find_shared_starts arguments:
- attendees: the people named. First names resolve when unique; the roster seen is Dana Park, Omar Haddad, Sam Ortiz, Priya Shah, Leo Chen and Ana Silva. The user is Maya Rivera and is added automatically, so 'me' or 'Maya' needs no entry.
- days: only the days in the requested window, as lowercase mon, tue, wed, thu, fri. 'Tuesday to Thursday' is [tue, wed, thu]; 'Mon or Tue' is [mon, tue]. Passing all five days returns starts outside the window, which must not be booked.
- minutes: an integer (30, 45 or 60 in the runs).
- earliest: HH:MM for wording like 'no earlier than', 'starting X or later', 'nothing before X', 'kick off at X or later'. Otherwise leave it as an empty string.
- latest_end: HH:MM for wording like 'wrapped up by', 'done by', 'finished before', 'over by'. Otherwise leave it as an empty string.

The procedure already accounts for everyone's calendars, time zones and notes such as Dana's 15-minute buffer, so do not read calendars by hand.

book_time: take the earliest day in week order that has starts, and its first start. Use the meeting topic as the title (for example 'Launch review'), the same minutes, and the same attendees, preferably as full names. Book once only. If no starts come back, do not book outside the constraints; tell the user or hand off. Reply with the day and time booked."""},
    {'name': 'book_several_meetings', 'description': "Requests for more than one meeting this week with the same group: 'two meetings', 'two sessions', 'twice', '30 minutes each', 'on two different days'. Not this kind: a request that says 'one meeting', or that names several people for a single meeting.", 'route': 'none', 'read_only': False, 'body': """This goes to the agent with the right to act, so do not mark it read-only. The single-meeting shortcut must not book just one.

The agent should call find_shared_starts once, with the attendees, the window days in lowercase, the minutes, and earliest or latest_end as stated (empty string if not stated). It then calls book_time twice: the earliest start on each of the first two different days that have starts, with the same title, minutes and attendees.

If fewer than two days have starts, tell the user rather than putting both meetings on one day or going outside the window. Low reasoning is enough."""},
    {'name': 'meeting_question_or_change_no_booking', 'description': "Requests that concern a meeting but do not ask to book a new one. Covers availability only ('when are X and Y free, don't book'), hypotheticals ('would Tuesday cause conflicts', 'would Friday be bad'), status questions ('is Dana double-booked', 'do I already have a sync', 'how long is it set to run', 'has Leo accepted'), what was decided or noted in a past meeting, and requests to cancel, move, hold off, draft invite text, or pass a message to someone. Not this kind: any request that actually wants a meeting booked.", 'route': 'none', 'read_only': True, 'body': """Read-only: never call book_time, and do not attempt cancel_event (it fails with 'not an event you booked for this request'). Pass to the agent with read_only true.

The agent may answer using:
- read_calendar(person, day): empty person is the user, empty day is the whole week.
- find_shared_starts for availability, with the days asked about, and 30 minutes if no length is given.

Limits to state honestly:
- Other people's events show only as 'Busy', or as free-type items such as Gym or Reading time.
- The user's own events have ids like E01 and are often just Focus time.
- The calendar holds only this week. It has no meeting notes, decisions or invite responses.
- A meeting to cancel or query may not be on the calendar at all.

For 'hold off' or 'draft' requests, acknowledge or write the text; call no action."""},
    {'name': 'outside_the_job', 'description': 'Requests that have nothing to do with scheduling a meeting, even if they name colleagues: ordering lunch, filing expense reports, pulling sales numbers, summarizing a document or deck. Not this kind: anything that asks for a meeting to be booked or asks about a meeting.', 'route': 'none', 'read_only': True, 'body': """Do not act. Hand to the agent with read_only true, and reply that this is outside what the calendar assistant can do.

Never turn such a request into a meeting. One run booked a 'Lunch for team' meeting for a lunch order and was rejected for booking a meeting nobody asked for.

Reading calendars is unnecessary here. Names in the request (Dana, Leo and so on) are not a signal to schedule."""},
]

async def decide(request, kit):
    found = await kit.recall(request, k=1)
    if len(found) == 0:
        return {"handoff": "nothing learned applies"}
    return {"serve": found[0]["name"]}
